Metadata.CommitMsg:
perf: read the leaderboard from the daily rollup, with the plans to show it

Adds tests/tools/sql_plans.py, which builds a throwaway database, loads it,
measures with EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) before and after creating the shipped
indexes, and drops it. The demo database holds ~2,600 idle events; at that size
PostgreSQL correctly sequential-scans everything, so plans taken from it would
prove nothing. The "before" case has the index genuinely absent rather than
disabled with enable_indexscan = off, because a disabled index scan falls back to
a bitmap scan and the comparison stops meaning what it appears to mean.

Three shipped indexes are transformative at two million rows: keyset pagination,
the partial excessive index and the per-vehicle history each gain two orders of
magnitude. One query was reading the wrong table.

The idle-cost leaderboard aggregated raw idle_events over a 30-day window on
every request. Its own docstring claimed the index narrowed the scan; measurement
showed the planner choosing a sequential scan, because a month of one tenant's
events is a large fraction of the table and no index fixes a query that has to
read most of the rows. In every run, with or without the index, that path stayed
above the 200 ms target. It now reads vehicle_daily - which already had an index
named vehicle_daily_leaderboard_idx that nothing used - and lands at ~100 ms,
about 3x faster, with non-overlapping ranges across four independent runs.

Correctness was checked separately from performance: the rollup ranking and the
raw ranking agree exactly on the demo data, 92 vehicles and 38,085.70 either way,
no vehicle differing. The cost of reading a rollup is freshness, so the response
carries data_through and computed_at, and the UI states the as-of date and says
the drill-down is read live - otherwise the two halves of the page can
legitimately disagree and look like a bug.

The method is the more useful finding. An earlier version took the median of five
runs and printed that single number, and the ordering of the two leaderboard
variants reversed between passes: one said the rollup was faster, the next said
raw was and even showed the rollup's own index making it slower. I wrote
"1.8x faster" into the docstring off the first pass, then over-corrected to "not a
measured win" off the second. Both were artefacts of five samples on a machine
contended by my own concurrent runs. Fixed by taking nine samples, printing the
full min-max range beside every median, refusing to print a ratio when the two
ranges overlap, and accepting a claim only once two independent runs agreed with
non-overlapping ranges. The narrative now asserts only what is durable and points
at the table for what is not, so it cannot contradict the numbers above it.

Also fixed: the report said "Table size: 0 bytes", because
pg_total_relation_size on a partitioned parent returns 0 - which reads as an empty
table rather than as the wrong function. Now summed over the partitions.

Adds docs/STRIDE.md: six trust boundaries, every STRIDE category, mitigations
naming the code and test that implement them, and the gaps written down rather
than omitted. Five open items ranked, the first being that nothing binds a
producer identity to a VIN, so everything downstream trusts that an event for a
VIN came from that vehicle. Every test name it cites was checked to exist.
